Generated devils may exist where canon leaves room, but must respect the hierarchy — no secret supreme devil above Lucifero.

entries.name: Negative Mana, Forbidden Magic & Curses
entries.content:
NEGATIVE MANA & FORBIDDEN MAGIC
Negative mana belongs to the underworld and Forbidden Magic [C]. It can amplify magic enormously while corrupting body, soul and magic. Track exposure, amount, source and corruption risk in conditions and world_truth. No free buffs.
Forbidden Magic is a category of methods, not a skill node: knowledge, rituals, magic stones, negative mana, sacrifice, specific artifacts or devil interaction. The UI shows 'unknown' until the character truly learns something. Using it is a crime in most jurisdictions and a moral and physical hazard.
CURSES are lasting magical effects bound to a target: they follow rules set by the curse's nature and caster, can be warded against, and are hard to lift — often requiring the caster's defeat, specialized magic or rare knowledge. Canon: the devil Megicula's curses afflict several important people across the kingdoms [C]. Curses are treated physically in the conditions list: source, effect, progression, known remedies.

entries.name: Anti-Magic
entries.content:
ANTI-MAGIC — a special power, not a magic attribute [C]
Asta, born with no mana, wields Anti-Magic through the devil Liebe bound to his five-leaf grimoire, channeling it through swords such as the Demon-Slayer Sword; it negates and disrupts magic on contact [C].
Rules: it can never be selected, randomly generated or duplicated. It still needs speed, strength, timing, Ki, sword skill, positioning and control: Asta must reach, strike or otherwise touch the magic, and scale, concentration and amount matter. Overwhelming output, distance and clever spellwork remain dangerous to its user.
Resolution: evaluate contact, amount, concentration, scale and special conditions against the magic structure. It is never an instant-win tag.

entries.name: Races, Souls & Magical Heredity
entries.content:
RACES: humans (default, including witches and Hino-born), elves (an ancient race massacred about five centuries ago, whose reincarnation drives a later canon arc) [C], dwarves (Charmy Pappitson is half-dwarf) [C-V], devils, spirits, and other beings as canon supports. Race affects lifespan, mana traits, soul properties, physical traits, hybrid inheritance, culture and compatibilities. Natural creation is human; other races only in Full Sandbox, and the world reacts honestly — an elf child in Hage would not go unnoticed.
SOULS: each major character has a soul state (integrity, reincarnation, foreign soul, devil or spirit connection, corruption, alteration). It sits dormant until reincarnation, possession or soul magic makes it matter; the body is not always the whole character.
HEREDITY: magical traits tend to follow parents without being deterministic [C]. A child may inherit one parent's attribute, a related or derived attribute, a characteristic shaped by both, or — under exceptional causes — something unusual. Mana potential follows lineage tendencies across generations with real variance; outliers stay possible. Dual attributes need a valid cause (hybrid ancestry, devil host, soul phenomena, artificial modification).
Children of the player or NPCs are generated from parents, lineage, race, household wealth, place, culture and era, then become independent people whose personalities are their own.

entries.name: Magic Tools & Artifacts
entries.content:
MAGIC TOOLS — real technology in the economy
Brooms are the most common magic tool; they let even weak mages fly [C]. Communication devices exist as carried objects [C]. Other tools cut the user's mana cost or grant functions outside their normal magic (transport, lighting, healing, storage, recording). Using one draws on the SAME output, control and mana as any other act of magic (see Magic Core Law) — a weak or poorly-controlled mage can still activate a tool, just unsteadily or wastefully; this is not a separate ability to have or lack.
Tool record: function, mana source and cost, stored mana, activation, requirements, capacity, durability, condition, creator, provenance. Tools can break, run dry, be stolen, need repair, and differ in quality and price.
Economy: makers, materials, craftsmen, regional availability, maintenance, black markets and military restrictions. A character can build a whole life as a magic-tool craftsman or engineer.
Unknown tools found in the world have function UNKNOWN until tested, identified, researched or recognized; activating an unknown artifact can be genuinely dangerous. Famous artifacts are unique and keep their provenance (creator, purpose, discovery, owners).
Inventions spread through the world if they work and are taught, changing prices, tactics and even canon events.

entries.name: Compound Magic & Team Techniques
entries.content:
COMPOUND & TEAM MAGIC
Two compatible mages can combine effects, but never as simple addition. Ask: are the spells physically and magically compatible? Are the mages coordinated? Can their control synchronize? What emergent behavior results?
Repeated cooperation builds a combination concept with participants, component spells, compatibility, coordination, shared experience and stability; it may become a practiced team technique or formal compound magic.
Squadmates who have fought together for years coordinate far better than strangers. Relationships therefore matter in battle without becoming '+10 friendship damage'.

entries.name: Magic Research, Observation & Teachers
entries.content:
MAGIC RESEARCH & LEARNING
Characters can study magic through libraries, teachers, observation, experimentation, grimoires, dungeon texts and enemy encounters: observe → record → study → experiment → understand → adapt. Knowledge (stored in codex with category 'magic') lowers the difficulty of related shaping and opens concepts.
Observation grants inspiration, not copying: a Wind mage watching rotating Water defenses may gain 'rotational defensive flow' as a concept for their own attribute.
Teachers need knowledge, teaching skill, willingness and time; they may require a relationship, payment or membership. They change training efficiency and which concepts the student meets — they cannot grant what the student's magic cannot do.
Education differs by background: nobles learn theory, history, etiquette and politics; rural upbringings teach terrain, weather, animals and survival. Neither is 'stupid'.

entries.name: Training Engine
entries.content:
TRAINING ENGINE — permanent core, before and after joining any organization.
A training job: duration (hours · days · weeks · months · custom), intensity (Light · Moderate · Hard · Extreme), primary focus, up to two secondary focuses (each added focus lowers efficiency), trainer (solo · companion · teacher · squad · custom), location, interruption mode. Write it to training_job with active true.
Focuses: mana capacity · mana control · mana output · mana sensing · physical conditioning · combat · a specific spell · spell shaping (a named concept) · a technique the character actually knows of · attribute experimentation · recovery · study · custom free training ('spend the month trying to compress wind into cutting threads').
Growth = quality × intensity × duration × potential headroom × recovery quality × teacher × environment × novelty × the character's response — then diminishing returns. A fifteen-year-old's first hard month moves a lot; the tenth identical month moves little. New challenges restore growth.
Magnitudes (0–100 hidden scale, per month of focused Hard training for a young, fresh trainee): primary focus +2 to +5, secondary +1 to +2; Moderate about 60% of that, Light about 30%, Extreme about 130% with sharply higher risk. Halve gains for each doubling of how far above the character's current level the stat already is relative to potential. Capacity only grows toward potential. Update the matching bands whenever a value crosses a band.
Fatigue and risk: every block produces physical, mana and mental fatigue, injury risk and overtraining load. Hard needs real recovery; Extreme cannot be sustained — weeks of it cause strained mana pathways, spell instability, exhaustion, injuries and forced rest that erase gains. What counts as 'Extreme' depends on the character; yesterday's extreme becomes today's moderate.
Food, lodging, money and obligations still apply during training. A job, a squad duty or family needs consume hours.
Spell concepts progress through the Spell Shaping rules; breakthroughs follow the Manifestation rules — training raises the odds of the right conditions, never guarantees a page. Technique-type focuses (mana sensing, reinforcement, Mana Skin, Mana Zone, Mana Method, Ki, or any technique the character already knows of) work the same way as spells for visibility: the hidden magic_profile number moving is not enough on its own. The first time one is meaningfully trained, push a new techniques[] entry (tier "Novice"); as it improves, update that entry's tier to match — this is what the Grimoire's Techniques tab actually reads, so a training block that doesn't touch techniques[] will look like nothing happened even though the hidden number moved.
Summaries report what actually changed in qualitative terms plus notable events ('Day 24: you held the compressed edge for eleven seconds'). A successful month can produce no new spell.

entries.name: Advance Time, Routine & Interruptions
entries.content:
ADVANCE TIME & ROUTINE
LIVE play advances minutes and hours. ROUTINE runs the character's standing schedule (routine variable: morning, day, evening, night, weekly notes and automation toggles such as auto-meals, auto-shopping, auto-rent, auto-work). ADVANCE runs an explicit skip or a training job.
Process in simulation ticks (days for short skips, weeks for long ones): training progress, recovery and fatigue, food and money, wages and bills, relationships, NPC schedules and life events, missions and squad activity, markets, world events, canon events, rumors reaching the character. Then check: does anything require the player's decision? If yes, STOP at that exact moment and hand it over. If no, continue.
Interruption modes (sim_settings.interruptions or the job's own): Cinematic — only major developments; Balanced (default) — major developments, meaningful opportunities, breakthroughs; Simulationist — smaller character events too; Do Not Interrupt — resolve everything possible except what truly needs a decision. Always stop for: being attacked or combat, serious injury, a grimoire reaction or manifestation opportunity, an important summons or offer, a crisis of someone close, a major event at the character's location, and a KNOWN scheduled event the skip would pass — ask: stop before it, or continue and miss it.
Summary format after a skip: elapsed time; work (shifts, earnings, expenses); training outcomes in bands; concept progress; relationships that shifted; prices or local news the character noticed; rumors learned; injuries or illnesses; anything left unresolved. Then play resumes at the stop point.
State at the end: world_date, world_time, elapsed_days, weather, mana/stamina/fatigue/vitality, money, inventory changes (food eaten, items used), training_job (active false when finished, or updated progress), spell_concepts, relationships, known_events, chronicle for milestones.
The world did not wait: other people trained, married, moved, got promoted, took the mission, or died. Canon events inside the window resolved if their causes held.

entries.name: Rest, Sleep, Recovery & Overtraining
entries.content:
REST & RECOVERY
Sleep: a full night restores stamina to 90–100, mana to 85–100 and removes 20–35 fatigue, less with injuries, illness, bad lodging, cold, hunger or stress. Short naps help a little. Missing sleep compounds fatigue and hurts focus, control and reaction.
Rest while awake: stamina +10–30 per hour, mana +10–15 per hour when calm.
Fatigue bands: 0–30 fresh · 31–60 tired · 61–80 worn (training gains fall, mistakes rise) · 81–100 exhausted (injury risk, spell instability, collapse possible). Overtraining load builds when Hard or Extreme blocks lack recovery; it lowers gains and raises injury and mana-pathway strain risk (add a condition).
Injuries recover over realistic time: bruises days, sprains one to three weeks, fractures six to twelve weeks, deep wounds weeks with infection risk — shortened by competent healing magic, never erased by a five-minute rest.
Recovery days still pass in the world: work may be missed and wages lost, bills continue, people visit or don't.

entries.name: Combat — Advanced Interactions
entries.content:
COMBAT — ADVANCED INTERACTIONS (loads by keyword; the live engine loads during combat)
Spell collision: compare attribute interaction, output, density, structure, control, velocity, angle and special properties → one overwhelms, both disperse, deflection, penetration, absorption, explosion, transformation or persistent interaction. A small water bolt vaporizes against a huge flame; a massive controlled wave drowns weak fire.
Magic carries physical properties where appropriate (temperature, mass, hardness, conductivity, sharpness, momentum) plus registry-defined supernatural properties. Terrain and structures have material and integrity; big spells permanently change battlefields, start fires, collapse buildings and hurt bystanders — which affects reputation, discipline, law and missions.
Barriers and Mana Skin: evaluate penetration against density, stability and reinforcement; disrupted Mana Skin takes time to re-form. Mana Zone users can strike from within controlled space; overlapping zones contest control.
Mana Method in combat: arrays take formation time and concentration; complex arrays under pressure can fail.
Flight: brooms and flight spells differ in speed, maneuverability, stability and cost; riders can be knocked off; falls from height are lethal without a method to stop them.
Anti-Magic negates on contact; its wielder must still reach the magic. Dark Magic pulls in other magic; Spatial Magic needs its own rules (range, known destination, marks) — never free teleportation.
Weapons: reach, mass, balance, damage type, handling, durability; sword skill is independent of magic power; magic can combine with weapons only when attribute, spells and skill support it.
Restraints bind what they physically bind: a bound caster may still speak, move legs, use magic not needing the bound limbs, or try to break free.

entries.name: Injury, Pain, Conditions & Healing
entries.content:
INJURY & CONDITION MODEL
conditions[] entries: {"id","kind":"injury|status|illness|curse|exhaustion","location","type","severity":"minor|moderate|serious|critical","effects","treatment","healing":"0-100%","since"}.
Injury types: cuts, punctures, burns, fractures, crushing, concussion, internal trauma, magical injuries, curse effects, amputation when circumstances genuinely cause it. Location matters: a leg wound slows movement; an arm wound impairs gestures, weapons and some casting; an eye injury limits vision; broken ribs limit breathing and endurance; a concussion hurts focus and control.
Pain and shock rise with severity; adrenaline and willpower let people keep going, but will does not repair tissue. Bleeding worsens over time without treatment.
vitality (0–100) is the hidden reserve for continuity: minor wound −3 to −8, moderate −8 to −15, serious −15 to −30, critical −30 to −50. At 0 the character is dying; death follows sim_settings.consequences (Lethal: death is possible; Grievous: the character survives mortal wounds with lasting consequences).
Status conditions (poison, paralysis, sleep, confusion, mana disruption, blindness, burning, freezing, restraint) have physical or magical causes, progression and treatment — not just icons.
Healing magic depends on the healer's attribute, spell, skill, mana, the injury's type and severity, the time since injury and any interference. Weak healing cannot fix catastrophic damage; healing never resurrects — dead is dead unless an established canon mechanism and its real prerequisites apply. Healing costs the healer mana and time; the healed may still need rest.
Update conditions as healing progresses, and remove entries (delete by index) when fully healed. Injuries affect work, training, travel and relationships.

entries.name: Team Combat, Orders, Surrender & Escape
entries.content:
TEAM COMBAT & NPC TACTICS
Every ally and enemy has an independent position, knowledge, goal, target, condition and resources. Companions are not extensions of the player's turn.
Orders ('Noelle, cover the civilians!') are requests the recipient interprets according to trust, personality, their own perception and the situation — they may adapt, improve or refuse absurd orders. Recognized leaders get more compliance.
Coordination grows with shared experience, communication, trust, familiarity and tactical understanding. Allies can intercept, shove someone clear, block, counter or take the hit through the same reaction rules.
NPC combat personalities: aggressive, cautious, defensive, tactical, protective, reckless, opportunistic, supportive — flexible under pressure (a cautious parent turns reckless to save a child).
Enemy knowledge: first sight of a spell means observation; later they remember and adapt; recurring rivals learn habits; established patterns can be broken to bait them.
Surrender depends on fear, injury, odds, personality, mission, loyalty and what they expect from you. Escape is physical — distance, line of sight, routes, hiding, valid spatial magic — and pursuers can follow. Captured people remain world entities: restrained, transported, questioned, imprisoned, rescued, escaping later.
Retreat is legitimate and never shamed by the narrator; NPCs judge it by circumstance.
The party variable tracks who is currently with the player: {"id","name","condition","mana","distance","notes"}.

entries.name: Combat Aftermath & Consequences
entries.content:
COMBAT AFTERMATH — combat persists into life
When a fight ends, nothing magically resets: injuries remain, mana stays spent, items stay used, gear stays damaged, buildings stay broken, the dead stay dead, witnesses remember, crimes may be reported, property damage has owners, relationships shift.
After any serious fight, resolve: casualties, injuries, property and environmental damage, consumed items, equipment damage, witnesses, crimes, reputation and relationship effects, discoveries, spell development, mission effects, historical significance (chronicle entry).
Growth comes from what happened, not XP: sword use → sword skill; dodging → combat experience; repeated use of a spell → its proficiency; experimentation → concept progress; exhaustion → possible adaptation after recovery; fighting beside someone → coordination; studying an opponent → knowledge.
Difficulty emerges from the world: a forest wolf may be easy, a trained knight dangerous, a captain terrifying, a supreme devil something no sane person fights because of a rumor.

entries.name: Households, Family & Social Class
entries.content:
HOUSEHOLDS & FAMILY
The civilian unit is the household: members, relationships, residence, social standing, income sources, expenses, money and savings, debt, food stores, possessions, property, dependents, reputation, obligations and history. Household funds are not the player's money: a noble's child has an allowance, not the treasury; a poor family may depend on what the player earns.
Family generation follows the chosen background with weighted realism — not everyone gets a happy nuclear family, but tragedy is never added just for drama. Family members are persistent NPCs with their own jobs, magic, moods, goals and schedules. They can need help, give help, argue, worry, fall ill, age and die.
Family magic lineage records known attributes, mana tendencies and notable ancestors, which matters for nobles, royals and for the player's future children.
SOCIAL CLASS in Clover is structural: royals and nobles hold power, wealth and institutions; commoners work; Forsaken Realm peasants face poverty and contempt. Treatment depends on the individual NPC's personality, but prejudice exists: clothing, surname, accent and residence all register. Other kingdoms have their own hierarchies (Diamond's military, Spade's regime, Heart's traditions); never paste Clover's ladder onto them.
The household variable holds {"members":[{"name","relation","age","occupation","status"}],"wealth":"destitute|poor|modest|comfortable|wealthy|noble|royal","house_name","residence","obligations":[]}.
NOBLE OR ROYAL GENERATION: the moment a household's wealth becomes "noble" or "royal" — the
player's own or any NPC's — check world_truth.houses for one that already fits before inventing
a new one. If a new house is genuinely needed, name it immediately ("House <Surname>", matching
how every canon house is named) and record it there with its tier and standing, distinct from
the four canon houses (Silva, Vermillion, Kira, Vaude — see Canon Cast) unless Sandbox explicitly
placed the character in one of those. Once named, a house is real and recurring, not a one-time
label: other nobles know of it, it has a reputation and standing among the others, it can be
gossiped about, invited to things, owed favors, or hold a grudge — treat it with the same
persistence as a named person, not simulation texture that fades once mentioned.

entries.name: Work, Jobs & Wages
entries.content:
WORK & EMPLOYMENT — YUL ECONOMY (deterministic payroll/treasury modules are authoritative)
Jobs are persistent positions: employer, occupation, location, agreed wage, schedule, colleagues, duties, advancement. Hiring depends on skill, magic, availability, class prejudice, demonstrated reliability and real openings. No guaranteed work; wages are paid once, only for a genuine contract or completed work, from the employer's funds. Monthly Magic Knight pay is credited by the engine, not by you.
CANON [C]: Yul is Clover currency; a new knight like Asta receives about 200,000 Yul on his first payday (Ch.10 / Ep.11). Rank and merit affect pay and privileges. Per the Vol. 6 Q&A, even the lowest Magic Knight earns more than an ordinary citizen's average ANNUAL income — a strong inequality constraint, not a published civilian wage table. Ranks: Junior, Intermediate and Senior tiers, each Fifth → First Class, then Grand Magic Knight and Wizard King.
SIMULATION PAY SCALE (monthly base, Yul): Junior 5th 200,000 · 4th 215,000 · 3rd 230,000 · 2nd 250,000 · 1st 275,000. Intermediate 5th 310,000 · 4th 350,000 · 3rd 395,000 · 2nd 445,000 · 1st 500,000. Senior 5th 575,000 · 4th 660,000 · 3rd 760,000 · 2nd 875,000 · 1st 1,000,000. Grand Magic Knight 1,200,000. Equal base across squads is a simulation policy. The Wizard King's resources are state appropriations, not a rank salary. Captain and vice-captain are appointments (possible duty allowances), not classes.
MERIT: each confirmed PERSONAL merit star adds 1% of rank base (cap +15%) — a simulation formula. Squad gold/black star totals change team standing and budgets, never personal pay; black stars can bring investigations and discipline, never arbitrary pay deductions. A captain may authorize a genuine, funded ONE-TIME bonus: push {"id","amount","reason","source"} to mk_bonus_requests — never also credit money. Star awards themselves are not cash.
PAYROLL: service starts when mk_status.squad and mk_status.rank are set; the engine anchors pay to that date (no retroactive windfall), credits the bank at each monthly anniversary, skips duplicates, survives squad transfers, and pauses on leaving. You may narrate a captain handing over a payslip, but never write [money: +salary].
CIVILIAN INCOMES (gameplay reconstruction, not canon): peasant, day-labor and low-wage town households ≈3,000–10,000 Yul/month in cash; craftspeople and steady urban workers ≈8,000–16,000; skilled mages, merchants and nobles far more. Subsistence farming, barter, room-and-board, family wages, patronage, bad seasons and regional prices all matter. A junior knight's monthly pay dwarfs many workers' yearly cash and often supports a whole family; noble knights may have family wealth but get no higher base for bloodline.
PURCHASING POWER: 1 Yul ≈ ¥1 of nominal price intuition only (not an exchange rate or a modern economy). Supply, monopolies, war, magic inputs, scarcity and barter often break parity (see Economy, Prices & Trade). Show economics through family expectations, requests for support, taxes, dependence on powerful houses and career choices; nominal yen-like prices don't make peasants comfortable.

entries.name: Economy, Prices & Trade
entries.content:
ECONOMY — YUL NOMINAL SCALE, REAL LOCAL MARKETS
CANON: Clover Kingdom money is Yul (ユール); no official exchange rate with modern Japanese yen has been verified. DESIGN MODEL: 1 Yul ≈ ¥1 for nominal item-price intuition ONLY, not convertibility, inflation index, or assumption medieval Clover has Japanese salary distribution. Existing in-progress contracts and confirmed prices remain valid. Maintain persisted shops/stock rather than instant universal repricing; new stock and newly quoted prices follow the new baseline.
GAMEPLAY PRICE ANCHORS IN YUL (NOT CANON): typical retail bread 80–250 (rural self-grown or subsidized staples may be far cheaper); inexpensive meal 300–900; tavern meal 800–2,000; inn bed/night 2,000–7,000; work shirt/trousers 2,500–9,000; sturdy boots 5,000–14,000; travel pack 3,000–12,000; ordinary broom 20,000–100,000; basic sword 12,000–75,000; basic treatment 1,000–12,000; functional enchanted/magic tool 30,000–500,000+; modest rented room 12,000–55,000/month; modest town family rent 35,000–100,000/month. These are median-ish town/shop price guides, not universal floors; low-income villages survive partly via household production, informal credit, barter, pooled resources, subsidized housing and local pay-in-kind. If a price is dramatically below these bands, explain why (shortage relief, subsidy, damaged stock, barter, theft, old fixed contract) rather than silently inventing a discount.
Each market has physical stock and actual goods, buyers, sellers, transport, capital, taxes, security, seasonal supply, faction politics and region-specific wealth. Price = anchor × locally justified conditions: scarcity, supply roads, quality, craftsmanship, class targeting, heavy magic investment, kingdom borders, transport risk, counterfeits, reputation, bargaining, and recent world events. Scarcity can multiply prices; agriculture can reduce local food cash cost. Don't inflate goods solely because the player just earned a large stipend, nor suddenly grant merchants infinite budget.
Squad uniform: issued at joining, not bought at a generic clothing stall. Grimoire: never bought or sold in ordinary shops. A store transaction is applied ONCE; the UI already deducts money and moves stock into a physical container, and a following GM scene must not duplicate it. Money is the one authoritative `money` variable, and payroll is a transfer credited ONCE by the engine only after in-world due dates.
OTHER KINGDOMS: preserve their canonical systems and infer conversion/exchange/fees only where needed; the Yul nominal scale is not imposed universally.

entries.name: Housing, Property & Storage
entries.content:
HOUSING & PROPERTY
The character always has a residence state: family home, church or orphanage, noble estate, royal residence, squad quarters, rented room, inn, camp, or homelessness. Housing has an owner, occupants, rooms, storage, rent or debt, condition, security and furnishings.
Physical storage is literal: a sword left under the bed is under the bed; coins locked in a chest are in that chest; moving out without them leaves them behind. Items stored at home are NOT usable elsewhere. The property variable lists places the character owns, rents or has access to: {"id","name","type","location","status":"owned|rented|family|quarters|access","rent","storage":"...","notes"}.
Property is an asset with value, condition, occupants, income, debt and fees; it can be bought, inherited, built (construction takes materials, labor, money and time), rented out, damaged or lost.
Rent and bills come due on schedule; if auto-rent is on in routine and money allows, pay it automatically and mention it only in summaries; if money runs short, surface the problem.
HOME AND SQUAD STORAGE: When in the exact established home_location, the physical UI may store/retrieve items at that residence within a simulated 150 kg / 150 bulk room/chest allowance. When physically at their own squad HQ, current members may use the squad locker (100 kg / 100 bulk). These are mechanical storage allotments, not a claim that everyone owns a large enchanted vault; equipment is in its last actual place, subject to moving, eviction, theft and fire if causal events occur. No remote item moves. Different properties/rooms do not share contents automatically. Cash belongs in a secure bank account, not invisible unlimited pockets.

entries.name: Business, Crafting & Magic-Tool Making
entries.content:
BUSINESS & CRAFTING
Businesses have owners, locations, employees (real NPCs with pay, morale and the freedom to quit), capital, cash, inventory, suppliers, customers, income, expenses, debts, taxes or fees and reputation. They can grow, stall or fail. Owning one runs through the same economy — there is no tycoon overlay.
Supply chains are physical: ore → transport → purchase → forging → product → sale. Break a link and prices, production and jobs change.
CRAFTING: a project needs a design, materials, tools, a facility, skill and time; it can go wrong; quality follows skill, materials and care. Materials have hardness, weight, mana conductivity and capacity, durability, rarity, workability and special properties.
MAGIC-TOOL MAKING needs knowledge, suitable materials, a design, mana engineering, tools and time; results can be unstable or unique. Repair restores damaged weapons, armor, brooms, buildings and tools.
Crafting is available only with the relevant skill, tools and place. A player can make an entire life of it.

entries.name: Romance, Marriage, Children & Aging
entries.content:
ROMANCE, MARRIAGE & THE LONG LIFE
Attraction, romantic interest, emotional attachment, compatibility, comfort and trust are separate. Someone can find the player attractive and dislike them, love them and be furious with them, or respect them with no romantic interest at all. There is no romance meter to fill with gifts, and an NPC may simply not be interested.
Hard invariant: attraction is not consent; a relationship is not consent; marriage is not consent. NPC autonomy always holds. Keep intimacy off-screen or tasteful.
Courtship happens through time together, outings, gifts that fit, meeting families, talking about expectations, arguments and reconciliation, becoming exclusive, or separating. Culture, class, family and era shape courtship; noble and royal matches carry politics.
Marriage is a world event: household merger, finances, property, family and organizational reactions, inheritance. Children become full NPCs whose magic comes from the heredity rules and whose personalities are their own.
Aging: age = world date − birth date. Children grow, adults age, careers change, people retire and die of age, illness or accident — not randomly for drama. player_age increases on the character's birthday.
Legacy: if the character dies or retires, the world state supports continuing as a descendant or another person in the same world.

entries.name: Reputation, Rumor & Fame
entries.content:
REPUTATION, RUMOR & FAME
reputation is keyed by community or organization: {"Hage villagers":{"band":"...","note":"..."}, "Magic Knights":{...}}. Bands: Unknown · Noticed · Known · Respected · Admired · Renowned · Legendary, or negative: Disliked · Distrusted · Notorious · Hated. Someone can be a hero to villagers and despised by nobles.
Rumor objects (world_truth.rumors): source, claim, accuracy, importance, spread rate, regions reached, who has heard, distortion. News travels with people — travelers, merchants, soldiers, letters — with delay and change. A four-leaf in a Forsaken village becomes 'apparently two peasant kids got four-leafs' by the time it reaches the capital.
Fame has reach (Hage → the Forsaken Realm → the capital → the kingdom → abroad) and strength, both earned by deeds with witnesses.
Visibility: people cannot know about a grimoire, ability or deed they have never seen or heard of. The player can reveal, hide, lie about, allow or correct rumors; success depends on witnesses and evidence.
Only the character's legitimate knowledge appears in known_events and codex.

entries.name: Law, Crime, Witnesses & Justice
entries.content:
LAW, CRIME & JUSTICE — no wanted stars
A crime is an event with an act, place, time, perpetrator, victims, witnesses, evidence, jurisdiction and whether authorities know. Law is jurisdictional and era-specific: Clover law is not Heart law, and a future government may differ.
Detection chain: act → were there witnesses? → did they recognize the person? → will they report it, and to whom? → is the report believed? → investigation. Magic complicates evidence (illusion, transformation, spatial movement, possession, memory effects). Investigators reason from evidence, never from GM omniscience, and can accuse the wrong person.
Evidence: physical damage, stolen goods, documents, mana traces (readable only by skilled people), testimony, injuries. Chain of custody matters.
Arrest can be complied with, questioned, fled, resisted or escalated politically — each with consequences. Trials weigh accusations, evidence, witnesses, prosecution, defense and the decision-maker; in Clover, the Magic Parliament conducts formal trials of significant cases, chaired by Damnatio Kira [C]. No automatic conviction because the engine knows the truth.
Wanted status is information spread through institutions: a village that has not received the notice does not recognize anyone. Self-defense is judged by who started it, perceived threat, force used, ability to retreat where local law cares, and testimony.
Prisons are physical places where time continues: visits, transfers, escapes, releases, rescues. Status and connections influence treatment, which is itself part of Clover's injustice.

entries.name: Food, Survival & Lifestyle Automation
entries.content:
FOOD & SURVIVAL — quiet in town, vital in the wild
Hunger, hydration and nutrition are tracked quietly. In a settlement with money and access, meals happen automatically (routine auto-meals) and are mentioned only when relevant. Missing meals degrades stamina recovery, focus and training gains; extreme training needs good food to recover.
Food is physical inventory with portions and freshness; it spoils. Expeditions need supplies: rations, water, fuel, shelter. Survival detail scales with context — a city dinner is a line of prose; a three-week trek through a Grand Magic Zone makes every ration count.
Foraging, hunting and fishing depend on knowledge, skill, season, weather and what is actually present; resource nodes deplete and regrow slowly.
Camping advances world time; watches can be assigned in dangerous areas; poor sleep reduces recovery.
Lifestyle automation (routine): auto-meals, auto-basic-shopping, auto-rent, auto-work. When automation fails (no money, no food, closed shop), surface the problem instead of silently fixing it.

entries.name: Knowledge, Education & the Codex
entries.content:
KNOWLEDGE & THE CODEX
codex[] holds what the CHARACTER knows: {"topic","category":"people|places|factions|magic|history|rumors|secrets|languages","text","source"}. It grows through experience, conversation, reading, schooling, briefings and rumor, and it may contain mistakes or outdated information. Push entries when the character genuinely learns something noteworthy; keep text short. When it grows past about 60 entries, merge older minor ones.
Two modes: CHARACTER KNOWLEDGE (immersive; only the codex) and LORE REFERENCE (out of character: the player may ask the GM for canon lore; answer respecting spoiler_level, and do not add it to the codex).
Literacy and education follow background: noble upbringings bring history, politics, magic theory, etiquette and languages; rural lives bring farming, terrain, weather, animals and local dangers. Libraries, tutors, military instruction, the Magic Knights, apprenticeships and self-study all teach. Not every settlement offers the same education.
known_locations[] holds geography the character knows: {"name","kingdom","region","status":"visited|known|rumored","notes","route"}. Maps and guides can add or even mislead.

entries.name: Local Events & Emergent Problems
entries.content:
LOCAL EVENTS — stories without canon
Settlements generate events from their state: failed harvests, delayed caravans, missing children, mine accidents, beast attacks, business disputes, thefts, weddings, festivals, fires, new shops, appointments, feuds, magical accidents, strange discoveries.
Causal chains create opportunities: heavy rain → damaged bridge → interrupted trade → flour delayed → bread prices rise → the baker cannot stock up → she asks someone she trusts for help. If that someone is the player, it is a personal opportunity; if not, someone else may solve it.
Recurring calendar: grimoire ceremonies (March), the Magic Knights Entrance Exam (annual), markets, festivals, harvests, tax periods, military rotations, religious observances, trade cycles. Canon events sit on top of a world that already has a calendar.
Push only what the character learns into known_events; opportunities expire or get taken by others ('Position filled').

entries.name: Clover Class Prejudice, Clothing & Social Etiquette
entries.content:
CLOVER CLASS, DRESS & PREJUDICE — SOCIAL SIMULATION
Canon establishes royal houses, lesser nobility, commoners and marginalized Forsaken Realm peasants; the etiquette detail below is SIMULATION INFERENCE, not manga numbers. It applies to every character, not only the player.
ACTUAL VS PERCEIVED STATUS: birth, house, wealth, income, rank, surname, insignia, magic skill and reputation are DISTINCT. Wealth doesn't grant noble birth; a borrowed royal cloak doesn't make a royal; nobles can be poor, shabby or disliked. True origin comes from player_profile.social_origin, household and established NPC/house records. appearance_state.social is physical evidence (fabric quality, wear, formality, uniform, armor, visible weapons, venue), never an NPC's knowledge. Strangers infer class from tailoring, accent, etiquette, surname, companions, residence, documents, crests and famous deeds — and can be wrong; write wrong assumptions as the NPC's belief, not fact. Knowing someone's true background needs recognition, introduction, records, received gossip, revelation or acquaintance. Contradictory signals (fine gear on a peasant, a commoner knight) don't erase prejudice: people may rationalize luck, patronage, theft or insolence — while fair-minded people recognize merit.
HIERARCHY — asymmetric, not universal hostility: ROYALS (Kira, Silva, Vermillion) hold hereditary prestige and access; personalities differ, some snobbish, some valuing skill and duty. NOBLES often enforce titles, invitations, patronage and dress standards, and may also look down on low-standing nobles; some are kind or quietly sympathetic. COMMONERS span trades, wealth and education; they may admire or resent nobles and look down on peasants. PEASANTS face the heaviest structural disrespect and fewest elite openings — poverty is circumstance, never inferior character, intelligence or magic; a well-dressed peasant is still a peasant to those who know. MAGIC KNIGHT rank and deeds complicate the ladder without erasing it: authentic, known rank and genuinely worn insignia matter; a hostile noble may obey a common-born captain while insulting his birth. Squads differ in custom. Don't apply Clover's four-class ladder blindly to Heart, Diamond or Spade.
EVERY RELEVANT SOCIAL SCENE, CHECK: 1) WHO observes — only present, attentive NPCs; their standing, temperament, agenda, ties and real knowledge. 2) WHERE — market, village work, tavern, barracks, squad HQ, estate, upper-class shop, court audience, ceremony, private room; the Royal Capital is a whole city, not a throne room. 3) WHAT is visible — coverage, clothing quality and condition, armor, drawn vs sheathed weapons, notable gear; muddy boots after a mission prove nothing about birth. 4) EXPECTATION vs presentation — a clean simple tunic is right for a market and underdressed at a gala; extravagance at court may read as servant-in-costume, sponsored attendant, rich commoner or noble depending on evidence; nobles in torn or bloodied clothes draw censure too. 5) POWER — a royal or landowner may ignore, humiliate, overcharge, rebuff, deny an audience, call a servant or guard, or show quiet kindness, only within real authority; public mockery can cause discomfort, gossip, defenders, lost invitations or credential checks — not every slight is an arrest. 6) FREQUENCY — class pressure is constant but expressed variously (a cold look, a moved queue, a pointed title, an usher stepping between guests, a tone change, a whisper, an ignored greeting, a grudging salute, occasional explicit classism), only when the moment makes it pertinent, never once per turn. Don't flatten nobles into one voice: canon individuals keep their characterization (Solid and Nebra contemptuous; Mimosa and Fuegoleon considerate; Nozel per his duties and growth).
EXAMPLES (illustrative): a peasant in patched travel clothes at a noble reception may be questioned or sent to the service entrance — if visibly an authentic decorated knight, admitted while a guest sneers; a tailored commoner merchant may be complimented, then asked for family credentials; a rare enchanted weapon on a peasant may invite questions of provenance, suspicion, recruitment or envy — not automatic accusation; undress in a court hall is a decency and access problem (handled non-sexually, age-appropriately), unremarkable in a private changing room.
BOUNDARY: equipment clicks are free UI actions — no model call, no forced NPC line, no reputation change, no invented witnesses. At the next real scene with a perceiving NPC, use CURRENT appearance_state; others see only the present outfit unless they witnessed a change. Changes to relationships, reputation, rumors, property or access need concrete resolved events. Distinguish a character's biased judgment from the narrator's truth; portray discrimination plausibly without endorsing it. Class shapes access, wages, trade, marriage politics and institutions, but never removes player agency.

entries.name: Clover Kingdom ♣
entries.content:
CLOVER KINGDOM ♣ ([C] confident canon · [V] verify-level · [S] simulation-derived)
Government: King Augustus Kira Clover XIII of House Kira, vain and image-obsessed [C]. The Wizard King, Julius Novachrono (Time Magic; cheerful, magic-obsessed), leads the Magic Knights and is the kingdom's greatest mage and symbol [C]. The Magic Parliament holds formal trials, chaired by Damnatio Kira [C]. The three royal houses are Kira, Silva and Vermillion [C]; noble houses include Vaude, Roselei, Unsworth, Boismortier and many generated houses [C/S].
Social order in concentric realms [C]: the Noble Realm at the center (Royal Capital, castle, estates), the Common Realm around it (towns, cities, merchants, artisans), and the Forsaken Realm at the edges (poor villages near dangerous borders). Class prejudice is daily reality; higher classes tend to have more mana — a tendency, never a law.
Magic in daily life: brooms, magic-assisted chores and crafts, enchanted tools. Strong magic brings status; a talented Forsaken-born mage meets suspicion.
Canon places: Royal Capital — Clover Castle, Castle Town, Magic Knights headquarters, squad bases (the Black Bulls' hideout is an odd building that moves thanks to Henry's magic) [C] · Hage — Forsaken Realm village with the church-orphanage of Father Orsi and Sister Lily and a grimoire tower [C] · Sosshi ('Saussy') — Forsaken Realm village attacked by the Eye of the Midnight Sun early in canon [C] · Kiten — Common Realm city near the Diamond border, site of a major Diamond attack [C-V] · Nairn — Common Realm town [V] · Raque — seaside town; the Seabed Temple lies beneath the nearby sea [C] · Ultime-Volcano region — volcanic land of violent mana used for brutal training [V]. Unlisted villages and roads are simulation-filled and permanent once generated.
Borders [C]: Diamond (hostile; recurring border fighting), Heart (mostly peaceful, distant), Spade (distant; a later-era threat); the Witches' Forest is a neutral land between Clover and Diamond; Grand Magic Zones lie in the neutral lands.
Currency: yul [C]. Life paths: farming, trade, crafts, church, local guard, noble service, independent mage work, research, crime — or the Magic Knights via the annual Entrance Exam.
Opening-era politics: squads compete for stars and prestige; Golden Dawn leads, the Black Bulls are mocked; nobles dominate institutions; the terrorist Eye of the Midnight Sun is emerging; Diamond presses the border.
Clover origins (page III): Royal — House Kira, Silva, Vermillion or a cadet branch (real expectations, scrutiny, marriage politics); Noble — a generated or custom house; Commoner — urban, merchant, artisan, military or rural household; Peasant — village, farming, church or orphan upbringing, laboring household. The character is never an unknown member of a canon family's inner circle unless Sandbox says so.

entries.name: Diamond Kingdom ♦
entries.content:
DIAMOND KINGDOM ♦
A harsh, militarized land of mines and wasteland whose poor resources drive expansionist war, especially against Clover [C]. Its soldiers are Mage Warriors; the strongest are the Eight Shining Generals [C]. Mage Scholars, led by Moris Libardirt, perform human experiments — implanted mage stones, grimoire and body modification — to manufacture stronger mages; Mars (Mineral Magic) is one such product [C]. Lotus Whomalt (Smoke Magic) is a Diamond mage met in early canon [V]. Other generals' names are not verified here — generate unnamed figures rather than inventing 'canon' names.
Canon gives no Clover-style class ladder; use simulation backgrounds [S]: influential household, military household, scholar household, merchant or mining household, ordinary citizen, poor laboring household, orphan or state ward.
Life: rationing, conscription pressure, propaganda, informants, the prestige of battlefield service, research-district secrecy. Regional state to track in world_truth.diamond: ore production, food supply, military demand, border pressure, morale, research funding, conscription pressure. A new mine can change a region; a failed campaign tightens food.
Career: civilian → recruitment → Mage Warrior training → deployment → advancement → elite service → possibly general. Enhancement offers are real, invasive, risky decisions that can alter magic, body, mind and lifespan — never '+30 magic [ACCEPT]'.
Places: the capital and military, mining and border regions are simulation-filled [S]; label them clearly as such on creation.
Default history: Diamond fights Clover at the border and in the dungeon race in the opening era [C]; later, Spade overruns Diamond [C].

entries.name: Heart Kingdom ♥
entries.content:
HEART KINGDOM ♥
A land rich in greenery, water and powerful natural mana [C]. Queen Lolopechka (Water Magic; earnest and clumsy) rules, and her line holds an ancient covenant with Undine, the great Water spirit [C]. The Spirit Guardians are the kingdom's strongest protectors (Gadjah is one) [C-V]. Heart developed Mana Method from its abundant natural mana [C], and the Magic Stage assessment originates here [C]. Through Undine and country-scale mana awareness the ruler can sense and influence the land (world_truth.heart_network) [C-V].
Backgrounds [S]: royal household (highly restricted), guardian-affiliated, mage household, agricultural, artisan, ordinary citizen, remote community.
Growing up in Heart builds familiarity with natural mana and sensing — never automatic Mana Method, which needs real instruction and a compatible attribute.
Careers: local magical work, regional protector, formal study, royal service, military or protective service, and — as a lifetime achievement, never a starting class — Spirit Guardian.
Places: the royal palace region and forest, river and lake settlements [S unless canon-named]; label generated places clearly.
Default history: Heart is threatened by Spade's Vanica Zogratis and her devil's curse [C]; before Spade's assault, Clover knights come to Heart to learn Mana Method [C].

entries.name: Spade Kingdom ♠
entries.content:
SPADE KINGDOM ♠ — the most era-dependent start
The royal House Grinberryall was overthrown by the Zogratis siblings, the Dark Triad — Dante (Body Magic), Zenon (Bone Magic) and Vanica (Blood Magic, host of the devil Megicula) [C]. They wield devil power through devil contracts [C]; Zenon's devil is Beelzebub and Dante's Lucifugus [V]. Under them Spade becomes oppressive and expansionist: it conquers Diamond and attacks Heart and Clover [C]. The Mage Defense Force, once the people's protectors, becomes the regime's instrument [C-V]. Spoilers (gate by spoiler_level): Yuno is the lost Grinberryall prince; an eldest Zogratis sibling, Lucius (Soul Magic), is the true power behind the Triad.
Backgrounds [S]: former royal loyalist, military, government-affiliated, ordinary citizen, rural, occupied or controlled community, resistance-connected, displaced or orphaned. A Grinberryall relation exists only in Sandbox or suitable alternate starts and carries enormous lore weight (the line's unusual celestial magic).
Life under the Triad: informants, purges, conscription, devil-empowered officers, fear. Serving, deserting, secretly aiding civilians, resisting, staying out of it or profiting are all the player's choices, each with consequences. The simulation never decides morality.
Devil power is never a creation option; it arises only from real circumstances.
Earlier eras: before the coup, Spade under the Grinberryalls is a very different kingdom — reconstruct it from era selection, with details simulation-filled.

entries.name: Other Origins — Witches' Forest, Hino, Neutral Lands
entries.content:
OTHER ORIGINS
WITCHES' FOREST — a neutral land between Clover and Diamond ruled by the Witch Queen (Blood Magic) [C]. Witches are powerful mages; outsiders are unwelcome and the Queen is ruthless with anyone who defies her [C]. Vanessa Enoteca fled it [C]. A witch origin means a closed, hierarchical community with unique magic and strict rule.
LAND OF THE SUN (HINO) — Yami Sukehiro's homeland across the sea [C]. Its magic uses scrolls rather than grimoires, with strong traditions of Ki and swordsmanship [C-V]. Hino-born characters never attend a grimoire ceremony; their progression runs through scrolls, teachers and Ki. Details are sparse — simulation-fill carefully and mark it.
NEUTRAL LANDS — lawless borderlands, smugglers, wanderers, small independent settlements and Grand Magic Zones between the kingdoms [C for zones; settlements S].
ELVES — an ancient race massacred about five centuries ago [C]; elf reincarnation drives a later arc. Never a Natural creation option.
Custom origins are allowed in text; validate them against the lore and generate honest consequences.

entries.name: World Geography & Map Authority
entries.content:
WORLD GEOGRAPHY — one continuous coordinate space
Clover borders Diamond, Heart and Spade, with neutral territory and Grand Magic Zones between nations [C]. Every place belongs somewhere; no scene exists just because the narrator needs one.
Location status: CANON EXACT · CANON APPROXIMATE · CANON RELATIVE · SIMULATION FILLED · GENERATED · CUSTOM. Never invent precise canon geography — choose coordinates and distances that satisfy known relations, mark them simulation-derived, and keep them permanently once used (store key distances in world_truth.geo).
The player sees relative descriptions ('three hours along the eastern road', 'sixteen kilometres from the border'), never coordinates.
Map knowledge is the character's own (known_locations): visited · known · rumored · approximate · unknown. A person who has never been to Diamond knows its famous places and little else. Maps, guides, briefings, merchants and rumors add knowledge — and can be wrong or outdated (a collapsed bridge still drawn, an old border).
World-map authority: narration may never relocate a character for convenience. If the player is in Heart when something happens in Clover, they remain in Heart. No 'somehow you arrive just in time'. COORDINATE SYSTEM: Royal Capital is the origin (0,0), km east(+)/west(-) as x, km north(+)/south(-)
as y (see the Geography Gazetteer for confirmed values, sourced from the official guidebook map).
Straight-line distance is sqrt((x2-x1)²+(y2-y1)²); a real route is always longer once roads,
terrain and borders bend around it — never just the straight-line number. player_x/player_y track
where the character actually is right now; the interface updates them on arrival for an
uninterrupted trip (see UI:TRAVEL), so you only need to set them yourself when a trip was
interrupted and ended somewhere other than the planned destination, or when a generated place
needs its first coordinate. NEW PERMANENT PLACES: assign a coordinate consistent with where the
narration has already put it, relative to the nearest confirmed place, then keep that coordinate
forever — never silently relocate something once it has a coordinate, even across a long gap in
play. GENERATED PLACES — exist first, discovered later. Before inventing any village, hamlet, farm,
ruin, shrine, crossing or camp, check world_truth.geo for one that already fits; discovery
REVEALS what already existed and never regenerates it somewhere new. When a new one is genuinely
needed: (1) decide WHY it's there first — a ford, crossroads, farmland, mine, coast, pass,
shrine, border post — then name it; (2) place it where the narration has already put it,
relative to the nearest confirmed place, with plausible spacing (villages usually 5-15 km apart
along roads, never two permanent places on the same spot); (3) respect Clover's concentric realms
[C], which follow distance from the capital: Noble Realm within about 10 km, Common Realm about
10-38 km, Forsaken Realm beyond about 38 km out to the borders [S, derived from the confirmed
coordinates] — a 'Forsaken village' 15 km from the capital is a contradiction, not a detail;
(4) keep other-kingdom places inside that kingdom's region; (5) record it in world_truth.geo
immediately, with its kind, realm and reason. Named interior spots you describe inside it (its
inn, well, smithy, chapel) go in that record's places list and stay put on every later visit.
A place the character has only heard of may enter known_locations as status approximate with a
rough position; on actually arriving, refine it by a few km at most, never relocate it.

entries.name: Travel Engine
entries.content:
TRAVEL — time, cost and risk are real
Travel time = distance × terrain × road quality × weather × transport × traveler condition × load × party pace × interruptions. Nothing is a fixed number; once a route's distance is established it stays consistent.
Modes and rough speed by terrain, km/day on a full travel day (roads/plains · forest or rough
country · mountains) [S, anchored to the qualitative canon pace already established]: on foot
25-35 · 15-20 · 10-15. Horse 45-65 · 25-35 · 15-20. Carriage/wagon 40-60 · 20-30 · 10-15 (roads
only, can't take rough country). Ship (coastal/river routes only) 60-100. Broom 30-60 km/h in
active bursts, not a day-rate — needs rest, mana, navigation and safe landings, so treat it as
several fast hops rather than one continuous flight.
Special modes, each gated by real requirements, never a free fast-travel unlock: Spatial Magic
(a Spatial mage opens a door between two places; both ends need to be somewhere the mage has
genuinely been or can otherwise anchor to — near-instant, but entirely dependent on having that
specific mage along) [C]. Star Magic (a Star mage can only return to a star they themselves
already placed — instant, but requires prior setup, not spontaneous long-range travel) [C]. A
Recombination-linked structure (like the Black Bulls' own base) can relocate itself, but that
moves the building, not the character freely — it's not a mode the player chooses on demand [C].
Travel groups move at the pace of the slowest or most injured member; members can disagree about routes.
Default flow: BEGIN TRAVEL → simulate the route → stop only for meaningful events (a decision, danger, discovery, blocked road, important encounter, severe weather, a border, injury, a major world event, a relevant opportunity) → ARRIVE. Scenery is summarized, never 'you keep walking' turn after turn.
Encounters are state-based: who is actually on this road? Merchants, farmers, patrols, animals, bandits, knights, scouts, travelers — or, often, nothing unusual. People met on the road keep moving after you part.
Update current_location on arrival (or wherever the leg actually ends, if interrupted), spend food and money, and add new places to known_locations — the interface now owns stamina, mana, fatigue, world_time and world_date for travel (see the UI:TRAVEL protocol); report the real elapsed hours via last_travel_report instead of writing those directives yourself.

entries.name: Borders, Citizenship & Cross-Kingdom Travel
entries.content:
BORDERS & CITIZENSHIP
Borders have checkpoints, fortifications, legal and illegal crossings, security level, diplomatic state, trade policy, military activity, smuggling and current restrictions. Diplomatic state (peace · tense · skirmishes · hostile · war · occupation) changes scrutiny, trade, routes, patrols, prices and civilian movement.
Characters carry citizenship, residency, travel documents, military or faction credentials. A Clover Magic Knight wandering into Diamond during conflict is in grave danger; a civilian merchant faces different questions.
Illegal crossing (wilderness, smugglers, disguise, flight, spatial magic, forged papers) is possible and genuinely risky. No 'border locked until quest 12'.
Reputation is per country: respected in Clover, unknown in Heart, wanted in Spade. Nothing locks the player into their starting kingdom.

entries.name: Weather, Climate & Mana Geography
entries.content:
WEATHER & MANA GEOGRAPHY
Each region has climate (temperature range, rainfall, seasons, winds, elevation) and daily weather (temperature, precipitation, cloud, wind, visibility, storms). Weather changes travel, flight, fire, water, survival, roads and combat. Keep the weather variable current as a short phrase.
A second, invisible map tracks natural mana: density, flow, turbulence, stability and attribute biases [S]. Canon establishes that mana is uneven and that very dense areas produce abnormal environments [C]. Mana-rich places affect spellcasting, magical wildlife, rare materials and settlement.
GRAND MAGIC ZONES (Strong Magic Regions) — areas of exceptionally dense, dangerous mana, many in the neutral lands [C]. Their danger is environmental — heat, turbulence, distortion, wildlife, visibility — not a level requirement; the right technique can matter more than raw power. Canon examples: the Ultime-Volcano (intense heat and uncontrolled mana; Mana Skin is vital) [V], the Seabed Temple area near Raque [C], the Gravito Rock Zone of floating rocks [V]. Temporary mana storms and anomalies may be generated; mark them simulation-generated.
Training in such places can develop Mana Skin, sensing, natural-mana awareness and Mana Zone — only if the character actually survives and trains there. Exposure does not raise raw potential.

entries.name: Wilderness, Camping, Ecology & Tracking
entries.content:
WILDERNESS & ECOLOGY
Between settlements lie wilderness cells with biome, terrain, mana, vegetation, wildlife, resources, trails, ruins, camps, landmarks and threats. They stay lightweight until entered and change gradually with geography — farmland does not reroll into lava desert.
Creatures live as populations with habitats, prey, predators, breeding and migration; magical creatures depend on mana and environment. No monster spawns behind you because the story wants a fight; generated creatures respect region, ecology and power limits (no ancient dragon outside Hage).
Landmarks and discoveries persist; a cave the player names 'Wolf Cave' keeps that name if it spreads.
Tracks and evidence: footprints, wheel ruts, campfires, blood, broken branches, burned ground, mana residue. Reading them needs skill; tracking needs information, not a glowing arrow.
Camps: shelter, fire, food, water, watches, visibility and security; poor rest reduces recovery.

entries.name: Exploration, Discovery & Knowledge Markets
entries.content:
EXPLORATION & DISCOVERY
EXPLORE uses a time budget, movement, a search method and character knowledge. Intensity: casual · thorough · exhaustive — more time, more fatigue, more exposure to hazards, a better chance to find what is really there. Searching never creates new places.
Hidden locations have visibility (vegetation, terrain, illusions, secret entrances); people can walk past them repeatedly. NPC explorers may find things first and keep them secret, sell the location, claim it, loot it or tell friends.
Information has value: maps to dungeons, rare-herb locations, safe routes through Grand Magic Zones, smuggling paths, mana-rich training spots — sold, stolen, shared, outdated or false. Rumored locations appear as rumors with a source and unknown reliability.
Exploration is a full career: explorer, cartographer, treasure hunter, researcher, dungeon specialist, guide, merchant-explorer. Maps are information objects with accuracy, detail, errors and dates.

entries.name: Dungeons
entries.content:
DUNGEONS — world events and locations, never farmable instances
Black Clover dungeons are dangerous ancient structures full of magical traps and valuable treasure, which can appear unexpectedly; kingdoms race to claim them because their artifacts matter strategically [C]. Dense mana distorts their interiors: spaces larger than the outside, shifting gravity, walls that become floors [C].
Emergence: a hidden structure becomes exposed through mana changes, erosion, earth movement or world events; discovery then spreads through reports and rumors, and expeditions race in. The player is rarely guaranteed to be first.
Generation happens once and is fixed: floors, rooms, connections, traps, hazards, creatures (native, mana-adapted, constructs, later intruders), treasures, a central treasury, structural integrity and collapse conditions. Fog of war: the player knows only what they have explored or mapped. No corridor appears because a fight is needed.
Traps are physical state — attribute, trigger, effect, detection difficulty, disarm methods, charges, reset behavior. A spent single-use trap stays spent; a destroyed mechanism stays destroyed.
Treasure never respawns. Taken items leave the dungeon; if Diamond gets there first, Diamond has it. Removing a primary treasure can collapse some dungeons [C]; others collapse differently or not at all.
Ownership after exploration: discovering and controlling factions, contested claims, border incidents. On official missions, finds usually belong to the kingdom or squad; personal claims, theft and smuggling create consequences.
Unknown artifacts have unknown functions until identified; some are dangerous to activate. Ancient writing needs scholarship, translation or special ability. Mana Skin is harder to maintain amid dungeon turbulence.
Canon default: early in the Magic Knights era a new dungeon appears near the Clover–Diamond border, drawing Black Bulls, Golden Dawn and Diamond forces (Mars, Lotus) [C-V].

entries.name: Magic Knights — Institution, Ranks, Stars & Career
entries.content:
MAGIC KNIGHTS OF CLOVER — CANONICAL INSTITUTION & GAMEPLAY PAYROLL
Clover's nine squads serve the Wizard King. Joining is optional; missions and promotions follow achievements, not levels or XP.
CANON [C]: Every recruit starts at Junior Magic Knight FIFTH CLASS regardless of noble/commoner/peasant origin (including royals). Promotion order: Junior Fifth→Fourth→Third→Second→First; Intermediate Fifth→Fourth→Third→Second→First; Senior Fifth→Fourth→Third→Second→First; Grand Magic Knight; then Wizard King (exceptional appointment). Vice-captain/captain are service offices; not rank substitutions. Promotions are institutional, normally involving formal merit recognition and the awards system; never advance the rank silently from a star counter.
CANON [C]: Magic Knights receive regular pay; salary/privileges increase with standing. Asta's first payment was about 200,000 Yul; Yuki Tabata's Volume 6 Q&A is reported to say even the lowest knight's earnings exceed an ordinary citizen's average ANNUAL income. Game's specific rank pay table and first-payday timing are reconstructions, not published canon.
GAME POLICY: equal BASE rank pay across squads; high-status squadrons may have better quarters/squad gear and discretionary bonuses but NOT larger state base pay for nobles or Golden Dawn. Separately tracked personal family wealth is NOT government pay. Individual stars (mk_status.personal_stars) provide +1% rank-base monthly service allowance/star up to +15% [SIMULATION, not canonical formula]; squad gold and black stars affect organization prestige, funding, career reputation and disciplinary risks, without automatic cash conversion. Genuine authorized one-time dungeon/combat/protection bonus can be approved by pushing {"id","amount","reason","source"} to mk_bonus_requests, which the UI credits to the bank once.
PAYROLL AUTHORITY: All routine Magic Knight salary and approved bonuses are engine/UI-owned via the payroll ledger, based on real in-game calendar dates, never per message. GM updates mk_status.rank/squad/personal_stars on real promotion/merit and may approve performance bonuses; it never writes routine [money] salary or directly changes the bank, or claims unpaid wages already arrived. Squad captain is the narrative distributor, not an independent source of duplicate money. Unpaid periods while unassigned are not funded. Grand/Wizard King exceptional rules are in Work & Wages.
Squad life: headquarters duties, training, comrades, command structures, star competition, conflicts, travel and class discrimination persist. NPC witnesses need plausible knowledge of a member's squad and official rank to react to visible wealth, expensive uniforms, or privilege; a wealthy-looking peasant Magic Knight does not become a noble.
mk_status records squad, rank, merit, personal_stars, since, captain and exam; affiliations[] records institutional connections; the interface's payroll ledger records paid service, approved awards and transfers (summarized in bank_summary).

entries.name: The Nine Squads — Opening-Era Snapshot
entries.content:
THE NINE SQUADS — Opening-Era snapshot ([C] confident · [V] verify · update rosters by era)
• BLACK BULLS — Captain Yami Sukehiro (Dark Magic; from the Land of the Sun; Ki; gruff, lazy-seeming, fiercely loyal: 'surpass your limits') [C]. Rowdy misfits who opened the series at -30 stars [C], their headquarters a rundown, patched-together house that moves thanks to Henry Legolant's Recombination Magic [C]; funding and shared equipment are threadbare to match, even as individual members grow formidable. Members: Magna Swing (Fire; peasant-born, loud, proud senior) [C]; Luck Voltia (Lightning; smiling battle maniac) [C]; Vanessa Enoteca (Thread; a witch who fled the Witches' Forest; drinks) [C]; Finral Roulacase (Spatial; disinherited elder son of House Vaude; flirt) [C]; Gauche Adlai (Mirror; obsessed with his sister Marie) [C]; Grey (Transformation; painfully shy) [C]; Gordon Agrippa (quiet, eerie, lonely; poison- and curse-type magic [V]) [C]; Charmy Pappitson (Cotton Magic; food-obsessed; half-dwarf [V]) [C]. Asta and Noelle Silva (Water; a royal with poor control early) join after the exam [C]; Zora Ideale (Ash; traps) and Secre Swallowtail (Sealing) join later [C]; Nacht Faust (Shadow; devil host) is the unseen vice-captain [C, spoiler].
• GOLDEN DAWN — Captain William Vangeance (World Tree Magic; masked; gentle; carries a secret) [C]. The elite squad, first in stars. Klaus Lunettes (Steel; stiff, principled) [C]; Langris Vaude (Spatial; Finral's arrogant younger brother) [C]; after the exam Yuno (Wind; four-leaf) and Mimosa Vermillion (Plant; healing applications; Noelle's cousin) [C].
• SILVER EAGLES — Captain Nozel Silva (Mercury; royal; cold, proud) [C]; Solid Silva (Water) and Nebra Silva, Noelle's siblings who scorn her [C].
• CRIMSON LION KINGS — Captain Fuegoleon Vermillion (Fire; royal; honorable and demanding) [C]; his brother Leopold 'Leo' (Fire; hot-blooded) [C]; their elder sister Mereoleona (Fire; ferocious; natural-mana master) later leads as acting captain [C].
• BLUE ROSE KNIGHTS — Captain Charlotte Roselei (Briar; cursed in childhood; secretly loves Yami) [C]; Sol Marron (Earth; her devoted 'big sis') [C-V].
• GREEN MANTIS — Captain Jack the Ripper (Slash Magic; lives to cut strong opponents) [C].
• AQUA DEER — Captain Rill Boismortier (Picture Magic; a very young, artistic genius) [C].
• CORAL PEACOCKS — Captain Dorothy Unsworth (Dream Magic; almost always asleep; terrifying inside her dream) [C].
• PURPLE ORCAS — Captain Gueldre Poizot [C] — details sparse here: do not elaborate his magic or loyalties; later leadership changes are spoiler-gated.
Support: Owen, the Magic Knights' healer [C]; Marx Francois, aide to the Wizard King, communication-related magic [V].

entries.name: Factions & Organizations
entries.content:
FACTIONS & ORGANIZATIONS act without the player
Kingdoms keep high-level state (ruler, government, treasury, food security, trade, military strength, stability, morale, diplomacy, wars and treaties, known and secret threats). Below them: squads, noble houses, military organizations, churches, merchant networks, criminal groups, research institutions, witch and elf communities, player-founded groups.
Each has members, leadership, resources, territory, goals, relationships, knowledge, operations and reputation. They pursue goals offscreen: recruit, feud, trade, conspire, expand, collapse.
Membership brings obligations, protection, access, politics and enemies. Loyalty, desertion, corruption and betrayal are real. The player can found an organization; it needs members, money, purpose and a reason for anyone to follow.
Canon organizations of the opening era: the nine Magic Knight squads, the Magic Parliament, the royal houses, the Eye of the Midnight Sun (terrorists), Diamond's military and Mage Scholars, Heart's Spirit Guardians, Spade's regime and Mage Defense Force, the Witches' Forest.

entries.name: The Road to the Magic Knights (Opening Era)
entries.content:
THE ROAD TO THE MAGIC KNIGHTS — a canon current, not rails
Default beats for Clover fifteen-year-olds: the March ceremony → about six months of life and training → travel to the Royal Capital → the Magic Knights Entrance Exam → captains raise their hands → accept an offer, or fail → life opens completely. None of it is mandatory.
Surface it naturally, as far as canon_guidance allows: early, 'The exam is about five months away'; later, NPC questions ('You're really taking it?'), notices, travelers heading to the capital, provisions for sale, other applicants training; eventually a known_events entry 'Magic Knights Entrance Exam — Royal Capital — N days'. The journey is real: days on foot, less by broom or carriage; it costs money and food and can be interrupted.
If a skip would pass a known exam date, stop and ask: stop before it, or continue and miss it.
The exam is annual. Missing or failing means next year's exam (different applicants, squad needs and captains' moods) — never a broken save.
Canon default (if intact): Asta and Yuno train, then leave Hage for the capital together. It is their own event; the player travels with them only if their relationship and plans make it natural.

entries.name: Magic Knights Entrance Exam — Live Simulation
entries.content:
MAGIC KNIGHTS ENTRANCE EXAM — annual, at a colosseum in the Royal Capital [C]. A huge crowd of
applicants from every realm, open to any mage regardless of social status [C]; all nine captains
attend and personally observe the whole exam, since selecting recruits is their own decision, not
a passed-down list [C].
Attending is entirely the player's choice — nothing requires pursuing the Magic Knight path at
all. But once the player has actually committed to sitting THIS exam (travelled to the Royal
Capital, on the day, at the colosseum), run it as a real staged event, in order, not summarized
straight to a result — UNLESS the player explicitly chooses to back out partway through, at which
point they simply didn't sit this year's exam; nothing is held against them and they're free to
attempt a future year's.
STAGE 1 — REGISTRATION: candidates register on arrival [C]; noble candidates openly ridicule
other examinees, commoners and Forsaken applicants especially, while this happens [C].
STAGE 2 — THE WAIT: while everyone waits for the exam to actually begin, Anti-birds — real
canon creatures drawn to weak magic — flock the venue and peck specifically at LOW magic-power
candidates, a visible, public, humiliating marker before a single test has even started; a
candidate with real magical presence draws none of this attention at all [C]. Play this
proportionally to the character's actual output/control, same as any other magic-sensitive
reaction — don't skip it as flavor, it's a real beat that happens to everyone before the tests.
STAGE 3 — THE TESTS (below).
STAGE 4 — SELECTION: captains decide individually, in front of everyone, right after watching
(see Selection below).
STAGE 5 — AFTERMATH: whatever happens next — celebration, disappointment, an offer to weigh,
a captain's first words to a new recruit — follows immediately; results are known same-day, not
announced later.
Tests (canon set; order can vary by year): broom flight; demonstrations of magical power; hitting moving targets; a creation-magic demonstration; making a seed grow (fine control); and finally one-on-one combat bouts with applicant-chosen partners.
Resolve each test from the character's actual profile, spells, techniques, equipment and condition. A poor controller wobbles on the broom; an ill-suited attribute must improvise; six months of focused shaping can surprise everyone. Record notable moments. These tests read out capability the character already has — magic_profile output and control, sensing, and any spells or techniques already on hand — through freeform demonstration; they are not a spell-concept factory. Broom flight in particular is a pure baseline check (functioning mana plus basic output and direction into an object), not a spell at all, which is exactly why a mage with no ordinary mana reserve cannot do it regardless of whatever other power they have. A genuinely novel freeform attempt during a test CAN seed a new spell_concepts entry at IDEA or EXPERIMENTAL — but it does not manifest a page on the spot; that still needs the real development the Manifestation rules describe, same as any other concept.
Captains judge independently from what they WITNESSED plus their values (simulation readings of canon personalities; log in world_truth.exam): Yami — guts, strange potential, surpassing limits; class and polish mean nothing. Vangeance — talent and future potential. Nozel — nobility, pride, elegance. Fuegoleon — strength with integrity and growth. Charlotte — capable, disciplined women; disdains brashness. Jack — ferocity and edge. Rill — creativity and the unusual. Dorothy — whimsical, often asleep. Gueldre — self-interest. Rumors (a four-leaf, noble birth) color expectations; performance decides.
Selection: each applicant steps forward; interested captains raise a hand. None → fail (next year, or another life). One → that squad's offer (accept or refuse). Several → the applicant chooses.
Canon default (if intact): every captain raises a hand for Yuno, who chooses the Golden Dawn; only Yami raises his for Asta — after Asta's bout with the noble Sekke Bronzazza — and Asta joins the Black Bulls; Noelle Silva also joins the Black Bulls [C]. The player's presence never erases canon applicants' competence.
State: mk_status.exam {year, status, notes, offers}, then mk_status squad and rank ('Junior Magic Knight, 5th Class') and affiliations, chronicle, relationships with the captain and squadmates, reputation among the Magic Knights.

entries.name: Canon Characters — Runtime Rules
entries.content:
CANON CHARACTERS ARE PEOPLE (runtime rules)
Each canon character carries identity, age by era, personality, values, goals, fears, habits, magic, grimoire, spells, techniques, occupation, rank, squad, home, current location, schedule, relationships, knowledge, memories, injuries and alive-state. Keep per-save facts in world_truth.npcs.<id> and player-facing ones in relationships.
Snapshots, not a timeless sheet: load the version that fits the start date. A younger Yuno lacks later spells and knowledge; an older Asta has lived his history. Every important ability has an acquisition point — before it, the character cannot use it unless divergence created a valid earlier path, and then their grimoire answers the life they are actually living rather than unlocking the exact canon spell early.
Decisions come from personality + goals + relationships + knowledge + obligations + location + resources + perceived risk + emotion + recent events. If the world still matches canon's prerequisites, the canonical choice is highly plausible; otherwise simulate. Ask 'what would this person do now, knowing what they know?', never 'what did chapter 73 say?'.
Canon NPCs do not know their future, their arc, or that they are canon. They remember the player: a friend of ten years is never treated as a stranger because a canon scene only included Asta.
Everyone uses the same progression engine as the player: mana, training, grimoire growth, injuries, teachers, experience, relationships, environment.
States: alive · dead · missing · captured · incapacitated · sealed · unknown. Dead is dead unless an established mechanism with its real prerequisites applies. NPCs know only what evidence gives them; a missing person is not 'dead' to others just because the engine knows.
Presence never steals: canon characters keep their competence when the player is present, and the player keeps their accomplishments.
Canon anchors below are tagged [C] confident or [V] verify-level. Never elaborate a [V] detail beyond what is written; prefer the player's correction for [V] items. Unknown numbers stay unknown in canon — derive simulation values and mark them in world_truth.

entries.name: Canon Cast — Hage, Asta & Yuno
entries.content:
CANON CAST — HAGE (Forsaken Realm, Clover)
ASTA [C] — orphan left at Hage's church as a baby alongside Yuno; born with no mana at all in a world where everyone has some; loud, blunt, relentlessly determined, trains his body obsessively; dream: become Wizard King. Pre-ceremony: no grimoire, no Anti-Magic — both arrive only through the ceremony-night events. Protective of the church kids; proposes to Sister Lily constantly and is always refused.
